recipes.name: Tuna Garden Casserole
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound kale, stems removed and leaves coarsely chopped
1 (5 ounce) can tuna packed in water, drained

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 2 quart casserole dish.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil, add penne pasta, and cook 10 minutes or until al dente; drain.

Heat the oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Mix in onion and cook 5 minutes. Stir in the celery and bell pepper and continue cooking for another five minutes. Mix in the garlic, salt and pepper and continue cooking 3 minutes. Pour in sherry; stir in the kale and cover. Reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the kale has wilted.

Transfer wok mixture to a large bowl. Mix in the cooked pasta, soup, vegetable broth, and tuna. Pour mixture into the prepared casserole dish. Top with a layer of mozzarella followed by a layer of bread crumbs. Bake uncovered in the preheated oven for 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Tuna Garden Casserole
raw_recipe.description: This easy to prepare version of the classic tuna casserole contains leafy greens, bell pepper, and penne noodles. You can easily substitute the vegetables with what you have in the refrigerator.

review.reviewBody: Everyone liked it. I made a few minor changes for what I had on hand (& to make it Gluten Free To make GF I first sprayed glass 9 x 13 dish w/olive oil then put 12 oz Schaar GF penne pasta in the bottom UNCOOKED (GF pasta won’t stand much cooking). I sautéed onion, celery, red bell pepper, garlic together (still tender crisp), added salt, pepper, 1/4 C red wine (it's what I had open), 8 oz frozen chopped spinach, 1 sprig of fresh basil & 3 or 4 stems cilantro chopped and simmered on medium heat covered until the spinach was thawed abt 2 or 3 min. Next, stirred in about 1/2 of a small steamed cauliflower left from the night before along with the salmon. Spread the mixture evenly over the top of the uncooked pasta (in the casserole dish), poured 16 oz ‘Imagine’ brand Potato Leek soup on the top, next 1 ½ C chicken stock (extra b/c pasta wasn't cooked before hand), sprinkled top with a generous cup of Daia (nondairy) Cheddar Cheese followed by 1/3 Gluten Free bread crumbs. I misread directions - preheated and baked at 350 instead of 375 needed 30 minutes instead of 25 for the pasta to be cooked al dente, but then I put it in uncooked too. All in all my kind of recipe, healthy, easy, one dish, and liked by all! I gave only 4 stars b/c I think it needs more than 8 oz pasta & 1 can of fish per 8 people.

We enjoyed this recipe. In the past, I have used light tuna to make tuna casserole. However, just a note, white tuna made a huge difference! As another reviewer mentioned, I added 1/2 tsp of chili powder - nice flavour. The amounts of salt and pepper are not mentioned - I used 1/2 tsp of salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. I did not have kale on hand, so, as suggested by another reviewer, I substituted broccoli. I also didn't have sherry on hand, so I used apple juice. No vegetable broth so I used chicken broth. I only had about half the potato leek soup, so I added milk for the remaining. I also sprinkled parmesan cheese on top. These substitutions worked out well. My kids asked for second helpings!

This was easy and good with a little pre-prep work. I could not find the leek potato soup, so subbed with cream of mushroom(2 cans). Cream of celery would have worked great as well. I also used two 5oz cans of tuna as another reviewer suggested. I used some red wine that I had available in place of the sherry. You definitely should season to taste before adding cheese and breadcrumbs. I cheated and used one big pot and put in all my veggies at the same time, when softened, added the liquids, then pasta. Love the beautiful color with all the veggies. Thanks!

This was really good and healthy. My husband was surprised that it had tuna in it even though I doubled the amount. I used cream of mushroom since that's what I had on hand and otherwise didn't make substitutions. 
All 3 little kids ate it up without a single complaint, vegetables and all! THAT is what I call success! We had lots leftover and ate some for lunch the next day. Again no complaints!
This will definitely be a regular for us.

Good variation to the often boring tuna casserole with more veggies. I felt using boxed or canned potato leek soup led to a runny and bland flavor so next time I will either use my own homemade soup recipe or make a roux in place of it.
This was awesome! I used two cans of soup instead of broth and sherry. Also added one can of milk. It was nice and creamy.

I loved it. Just finished off eating it tonight. I found this recipe to be a great way to put kale into my diet. Very tasty. I tripled the garlic, doubled the creme soup (and changed to both mushroom and asparagus as potato leek wasn't available in my local market), and doubled the sherry (heck... a little wine is good, more is better!). I found the mixtures of flavors to be terrific - the sherry added a great something in terms of taste. I will make this again. I think it is a "base" recipe you can adjust easily to suit the veggies you have on hand.

Made this wonderful recipe. Used cream of mushroom soup,added dry mushrooms and used the hydration liquid as my broth. The cheeses I used were cheddar and mozzarella. Made my own breadcrumbs with olive and rosemary bread adding some dry Italian seasoning. This was so good. Give it a try and use what you have on hand. It is great as a leftover heated in the microwave. I needed to put this is a 3 quart size baking dish.

Delicious! Had to make changes according to what I had. Used 12 oz pasta, 2 cans cream of celery soup (did not have celery), used about 1 1/2 cups cheese, used chicken broth in place of sherry and veg broth, used 10 oz pkg of chopped frozen spinach and two cans of tuna. Used everything else as listed. Definitely a repeat! Only two of us, but I think it will freeze well.

I found this to be a pretty good dish...a little atypical w/o mushrooms, but interesting. It does need some extra spices to add some heat (garlic and/or onion powder, Cayenne pepper). I doubled the tuna. The dish remains moist and flavorful as leftovers. Skipped the breadcrumbs but otherwise followed the basic recipe. I will eat this dish again. Gave some to my 98 yo Dad for lunches. He liked it a lot. Barilla Plus pasta adds protein since the recipe is a little shy of desirable levels due to a pasta forward dish.

I could not find soup listed in recipe so go a can of cream of potato. That soup was only 10 oz can so I added some cream to make up difference. Also I did not have sherry so substituted some dry white wine. Easy to make although it did make a lot of dishes. But something different and very tasty, Will for sure make again!

I made this for the first time today. And other than I should have let the Kale cook down a few minutes longer, it was fantastic, I did have to substitute a Dry White wine for the Sherry, and added some fresh leeks to a can of Cream of Potato Soup, but I will be adding this one to the rotation for sure
I left out the vegitable broth.
Very tasty - this is a lighter dish and I have cut the recipe in half before. Definitely add more tuna- it needs it.

I needed to use dairy and gluten free ingredients. Used Imagine brand soup and dish ended up a little too soupy, I suspect because of GF soup. Next time will not add any broth and it should be fine. Great taste!!
Was a lot of work to make. I probably won't make again. Added more tuna than it said. Okay, have just had better.

This recipe was great! I had to substitute cream of potato soup for the potato leek soup because we do not have this readily available in our major grocery stores in Houston, Texas. Next time I will add 2 cans of tuna instead of just one. I love tuna casseroles and this was the best so far. My husband really enjoyed it too. It's a new and creative spin on the old traditional recipe. Will definitely make it again! Thanks so much for sharing.
